long_biography.plain_text:
Serge Varsano secured control of Sucden in 1988 by buying shares, particularly from company managers, eight years after his father Maurice died. Varsano had spent twelve years inside the family company, advancing from commodity trader to sugar-division manager and chief executive. The purchases made him principal shareholder as well as the operating successor.

When broad diversification produced losses, Varsano pulled Sucden back towards sugar and sold peripheral activities. He then rebuilt the business around long-term supply relationships, with trading supported by production, processing and risk management. Varsano continues to chair the management board, whose mandate covers the group's major executive decisions, while general managers handle distinct operating responsibilities.
